text:
marta: Quick sync  we need final competitive battlecard language for the Thurs webinar + launch posts. Focus: cloud AI platforms, LLM API providers, infra vendors. Need: 3 crisp claims + 1-line proof, 2 inbound hooks for SDRs, and one webinar slide. Can we land this today?

shannon: Use claim / evidence / customer impact. Short lines. Example: 'Predictable inference economics' / 'reserved pools + batching saved 30% in typical chat mixes' / 'lowers cost per conversation.'

ana: Keep competitor names out. Proofs should point to product capabilities: Dedicated SLA pools, private VPC, and per-route cost analytics.

ana: Draft claims: 
1) "Predictable production performance across hosted, dedicated, and private"  proof: "SLA-backed dedicated pools + smart routing with compatible fallbacks." 
2) "Lower cost per conversation for chat workloads"  proof: "batching + KV prefix caching plus Optimize recommendations." 
3) "Enterprise controls without heavy infra lift"  proof: "Private control plane, KMS/HSM support, audit logs, on-prem option."

priya: Great. For the webinar slide pair each claim with a top objection + rebuttal. E.g. Objection: 'Cloud vendor has scale' -> Rebuttal: 'Scale doesn't guarantee predictable latency or cost; our routing + reserved pools do.'

shannon: Add one defensible benchmark line: "In internal chat benchmarks (mixed context), dedicated pools + batching gave ~2040% token-cost savings and lower median latency vs shared-hosted baseline." Frame as typical, not guaranteed.

marta: SDR routing hooks (short): 
- Cloud AI leads: "Want predictable latency and cost beyond raw capacity? 1-page economics comp."
- LLM API leads: "Need rollout control and private deploys? 30m demo of Dedicated + Private."
- Infra vendor leads: "Want low-level controls without hiring an infra team? We combine runtime control + ops tooling."

priya: Two email subjects + ABs:
A1: "Production-grade LLM inference without re-architecting your stack"
A2: "Reduce inference cost and guarantee latency  30m demo"
B1: "Benchmarks that matter: latency, cost, and enterprise controls"
B2: "Stop trading reliability for cost: predictable inference"

shannon: One-pager sections: claims (3), two-line proofs, top 4 rebuttals, routing hooks, anonymous customer line. Keep it skimmable.

marta: @ana can you draft the one-pager by EOD? Need to hand to SDR lead tonight.

ana: On it. I'll post a single-slide draft with bullets and rebuttals: https://redwood.internal/briefs/competitive-bc-draft.

priya: I'll map routing triggers and add 3 quick SDR scripts + an escalation checklist (scripts are 12 lines each).

devops-bot: Reminder: webinar landing page deploy scheduled 2026-04-02T16:00Z; CI smoke tests 03:30 UTC.

marta: Final checklist: Ana one-pager by EOD, marketing social hooks (I'll do), SDR routing confirmation (Priya), legal claims review (I'll ping). Review at 4pm PT. :thumbsup:
